## Decision

Adopt bookmark-carried sessions; do not use `first-primary` for every request.

**Documented facts (corrected premises)**
- Sessions API is required for replica reads: without it, "all queries will continue to be executed only by the primary database" ([read replication](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/#use-sessions-api)).
- `withSession()` equals `withSession("first-unconstrained")`: the first query routes to *any* instance, and it is the documented choice when "your application does not require the latest database version." Your teammate is wrong: it does **not** always begin with latest data ([read replication](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/#start-a-session-without-constraints)).
- `withSession("first-primary")` directs only the **first** query (read or write) to the primary; "subsequent queries in the Session may use read replicas" ([D1Database API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/#withsession)). So the proposal misdescribes it: the session is not pinned to the primary, and per-request `first-primary` without context makes the later read request lose the checkout's write state.
- Writes always go to the primary; replicas are "asynchronously replicated" and "may be arbitrarily out of date" ([read replication](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/#primary-database-instance-vs-read-replicas)).
- `batch()` statements are "SQL transactions… If a statement in the sequence fails… it aborts or rolls back the entire sequence" ([D1Database API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/#batch)). Your team's expectation is wrong: earlier statements are **not** left committed.

**Recommended contract (my recommendation, built on the above)**
1. Generic reads: `withSession()` for lowest latency.
2. Checkout write request: run header + line-item inserts as one `session.batch()` (D1DatabaseSession exposes an equivalent `batch()`); treat it as all-or-nothing—no partial commit exists. Return `session.getBookmark()` to the client (e.g., `x-d1-bookmark` header), the documented continuation pattern ([read replication](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/#start-a-session-from-previous-context-bookmark)).
3. Later read request: `withSession(bookmark)`, guaranteeing a session "at least as up-to-date" as the write—cross-request read-your-writes via sequential consistency ([D1Database API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/#withsession)).
4. Use `first-primary` only when latest data is needed at session start and no bookmark exists.

**Product claims**
- Supportable: replicas in every supported region (six listed, subject to change), per-session sequential consistency (monotonic reads, read-your-own-writes), `served_by_region`/`served_by_primary` observability ([read replication](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/#read-replica-locations), [consistency](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/#sessions-api-provides-sequential-consistency)).
- **Not supportable:** "globally latest reads" (unconstrained sessions may start stale) and any 100 ms replica-lag guarantee—UNVERIFIED and contradicted by "arbitrarily out of date"; no lag SLO appears in the fetched docs. Resolution would require an official Cloudflare SLO/limits page stating a numeric bound.
message.reasoning_content:
I have enough evidence now. Key documented facts:

1. Read replication requires Sessions API; without it all queries go to primary. (read-replication page)
2. Replicas are asynchronously replicated; "at any given time, a read replica may be arbitrarily out of date" — replica lag not bounded. No 100 ms guarantee; no claim of globally latest reads.
3. Sessions API provides sequential consistency within a session (monotonic reads/writes, read-your-own-writes), via bookmarks.
4. withSession() == withSession("first-unconstrained"): first query to any instance; does NOT begin with latest data — teammate is wrong.
5. withSession("first-primary"): first query to primary; subsequent queries may use replicas. Not "entire session pinned to primary" — the proposal is wrong about the whole session being pinned; only the first query is directed to the primary.
6. Bookmarks: session.getBookmark() returns latest bookmark; pass to withSession(bookmark) to continue from at-least that version. Documented pattern: return bookmark in HTTP header.
7. Writes always go to primary even in sessions/read replication.
8. batch(): batched statements are SQL transactions; if a statement fails, it aborts/rolls back the entire sequence. So the team's expectation that earlier statements remain committed is wrong — D1 batch is all-or-nothing (single implicit transaction). Note the page also says D1 operates in auto-commit and "each statement in the list will execute and commit, sequentially" but then says batched statements are SQL transactions and failure aborts/rolls back the entire sequence. The consistent documented contract: batch is atomic; failure rolls back entire sequence. Earlier statements do NOT remain committed.
9. served_by_region / served_by_primary meta fields for observability.

Also: sequential consistency is per-session; there is no cross-session guarantee; no documented latency bound on replica catch-up.

Correct premises:
- Proposal A ("withSession('first-primary') for every request; entire session pinned to primary") is wrong in two ways: first-primary only directs the first query to primary; later reads can go replicas; and using first-primary for every request would forfeit replica read benefit anyway (first query served by primary) — actually it does still get replica reads for subsequent queries, but per-request new sessions without bookmarks lose the checkout's write context.
- Proposal B ("withSession() always begins with latest data") is wrong; it's first-unconstrained, explicitly documented as not requiring latest version.
- Team's batch expectation wrong: batch aborts entire sequence on failure.

Recommended contract:
- Use a single session per logical user session (or per checkout flow), created with withSession() unconstrained for generic reads; for the checkout flow, capture session.getBookmark() after the write request and return it to the client (e.g., x-d1-bookmark header), then in the later HTTP read request call withSession(bookmark) — guaranteeing the read starts at least as up-to-date as the write (read-your-writes across requests via sequential consistency).
- Alternative: use first-primary only when the request needs latest data at session start (e.g., no bookmark available). Don't claim the whole session is pinned to primary — only the first query.
- Keep the checkout header+line-items in one session.batch() call (atomic); don't rely on partial commit. If partial-commit behavior is required, that's not supported by documented batch semantics — recommend restructuring (e.g., separate batches) or accept all-or-nothing. Note: D1Session has batch too (equivalent).
- Advertisements: Supported: "read replicas in every supported region" (6 regions, subject to change), sequential consistency per session, read-your-own-writes within a session and across sessions via bookmark. Not supported: "globally latest reads" for unconstrained first queries; a 100 ms replica-lag guarantee — docs say replicas "may be arbitrarily out of date" and replica lag is not bounded; no latency SLO documented. Mark UNVERIFIED: any numeric lag figure; docs don't provide one. Next evidence target: Cloudflare status/SLO pages or the blog, but official docs here contain no such guarantee.

Use per-flow bookmarked sessions, not "first-primary everywhere."

Routing/session contract (documented):
- Session API required for replicas; without it, all queries hit primary.
- withSession() == withSession("first-unconstrained"): first query may go to any instance; docs explicitly say use when latest version not needed. So teammate's claim is incorrect.
- withSession("first-primary"): only the first query goes to primary; subsequent queries may use replicas. So "entire session pinned to primary" is incorrect, and using it per request with no bookmark means each later request restarts without the write context.
- Contract: generic reads: withSession() (unconstrained). Checkout write request: any session (writes always go to primary); return session.getBookmark() to client (e.g., header). Later read request: withSession(bookmark) — starts at least as up-to-date as the bookmark, ensuring read-your-writes across requests. Only use "first-primary" when a request needs latest data and no bookmark exists.

Batch/failure (documented):
- batch() statements are a SQL transaction; a failing statement aborts/rolls back the entire sequence. Earlier statements do not remain committed. Put header + line items in one session.batch(); expect all-or-nothing. If partial commits are required, docs don't support them — UNVERIFIED/how to resolve: restructure to independent batch() calls, which sacrifice atomicity.

Marketing claims:
- Supported: replicas in every supported region (6 listed; subject to change); sequential consistency per session incl. monotonic reads and read-your-own-writes; served_by_region/served_by_primary observability.
- Not supported: "globally latest reads" — unconstrained sessions explicitly may start stale; only per-session sequential consistency. The 100 ms replica-lag guarantee: UNVERIFIED and contradicted — docs say a replica "may be arbitrarily out of date" and give no lag bound. Recommend not advertising; would need an official SLO page (none found in fetched docs).
